title: Lifting a bounded-above acyclic complex through an ideal
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, let $I \subset R$ be an ideal, and let $\mathcal{P}$ be a class of $R$-modules. Assume: (1) every $P \in \mathcal{P}$ is projective; (2) if $P_1 \in \mathcal{P}$ and $P_1 \oplus P_2 \in \mathcal{P}$, then $P_2 \in \mathcal{P}$; and (3) every map $P_1 \to P_2$ between members of $\mathcal{P}$ that is surjective modulo $I$ is surjective. If $E^\bullet$ is a bounded-above acyclic complex of $R/I$-modules [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] whose terms are each isomorphic to $P/IP$ for some $P \in \mathcal{P}$, then there exists a bounded-above acyclic complex $A^\bullet$ with all terms in $\mathcal{P}$ and an isomorphism $A^\bullet/IA^\bullet \cong E^\bullet$ of complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules].

proof.text: Choose $b$ with $E^i=0$ for $i>b$; for $n>b$ start with the zero tail. Inductively suppose a tail $P^n\to P^{n+1}\to\cdots\to P^b$ has been constructed, with a morphism of complexes to $E^\bullet$, all $P^i\in\mathcal P$, the maps $P^i/IP^i\to E^i$ isomorphisms, and exactness in degrees $\geq n+1$. Working down from degree $b$, exactness and projectivity (1) split each short exact sequence of cycles and boundaries, so one can choose isomorphisms $P^i\cong Z^i\oplus Z^{i+1}$ under which $P^i\to P^{i+1}$ is the projection onto $Z^{i+1}$ followed by the inclusion into $Z^{i+1}\oplus Z^{i+2}$. Starting from $Z^{b+1}=0$ and applying (2) inductively from the top, every $Z^i$ lies in $\mathcal P$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.75.1, proof, construction of the split tail

proof.text: Choose $P^{n-1}\in\mathcal P$ and an isomorphism $P^{n-1}/IP^{n-1}\cong E^{n-1}$, which exists because $E^{n-1}$ has the required form. Since $Z^n$ is a direct summand of $P^n$ and the image of $Z^{n}\oplus Z^{n+1}\to Z^{n+1}\oplus Z^{n+2}$ is $Z^{n+1}$, exactness of $E^\bullet$ at $E^n$ identifies $\operatorname{im}(E^{n-1}\to E^n)$ with $Z^n/IZ^n\subset P^n/IP^n\cong E^n$. As $P^{n-1}$ is projective (1), lift the composite $P^{n-1}\to E^{n-1}\to E^n$, which lands in $Z^n/IZ^n$, to a map $P^{n-1}\to Z^n$. Its reduction modulo $I$ is surjective and $P^{n-1},Z^n\in\mathcal P$, so by (3) it is surjective. Appending $P^{n-1}\to Z^n\subset P^n$ to the tail gives a morphism of complexes to $E^\bullet$ extending the diagram one degree to the left, with kernel of $P^n\to P^{n+1}$ equal to $Z^n$ equal to the image of $P^{n-1}$; so exactness holds in all degrees $\geq n$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.75.1, proof, lifting the next term

proof.text: Repeat the preceding extension for $n=b+1,b,b-1,\dots$. Since each step only adds a term on the left, the descending construction defines one complex $A^\bullet$ with $A^i=0$ for $i>b$, every term in $\mathcal P$, and reduction maps giving an isomorphism of complexes $A^\bullet/IA^\bullet\cong E^\bullet$. Exactness in each degree was established when the degree to its left was added, so $A^\bullet$ is acyclic. Thus $A^\bullet$ is the required bounded-above acyclic lift.

lean.statement: theorem exists_acyclic_lift_mod_ideal (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (P : ModuleCat.{max u v} R → Prop) (hprojective : ∀ M, P M → Projective M) (hsummand : ∀ M₁ M₂ M₁₂ : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, P M₁ → P M₁₂ → Nonempty (M₁₂ ≅ ModuleCat.of R (M₁ × M₂)) → P M₂) (hsurjective : ∀ (M₁ M₂ : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (f : M₁ ⟶ M₂), P M₁ → P M₂ → Function.Surjective ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).map f) → Function.Surjective f) (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R ⧸ I)) ℤ) (hbounded : ∃ b : ℤ, E.IsStrictlyLE b) (hacyclic : E.Acyclic) (hterms : ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, P M ∧ Nonempty ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).obj M ≅ E.X i)) : ∃ A : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ, (∃ b : ℤ, A.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧ A.Acyclic ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, P (A.X i)) ∧ Nonempty (((ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj A ≅ E)
